summary: We have developed a website that inspires young people to explore the hidden stories in space. It addresses the challenge by showing every forgotten piece of equipment, its own interesting story, and its role in helping us understand space and get closer to new discoveries. Our development is very important because it helps and guides young people and even adults to get closer to NASA discoveries and the stories of forgotten objects.
details:
What it does & how it works:

Abandoned, Not Forgotten started to bring forgotten stories back to life. It’s an interactive digital archive that shows the hardware and tools left behind on the Moon and Mars-browsing missions in the Explorer, reading through detailed field notes in the Archive, testing their curiosity in the Mission Lab, and even leaving their own footprint before they leave. Every single timeline, fact, and technical spec comes straight from official NASA records, so the storytelling is easy to connect with.

Benefits & intended impact:

To a lot of young people, space history feels like a textbook full of distant dates and numbers. We wanted to flip that completely. By turning overlooked rovers and instruments into relatable human stories, we show how every single piece helped us understand our place in the universe. Our goal is to inspire young people to explore the hidden stories behind these objects.

Tools, languages, and software used:

We built the entire platform from the ground up using core front-end web technologies-HTML, CSS, and JavaScript-alongside HTML interactive visual elements and GitHub Pages for live hosting. We also relied on official NASA archives and databases as our primary research software and data sources, and used AI tools to help structure and refine our development workflow.

How our project is creative:

The real creativity wasn't just in the code-it was in how we looked at the subject. Instead of treating old space missions as broken machines, we reframed them as "off-world heritage": living proof of what humans can achieve when they refuse to stop exploring. By mixing interactive features like the Mission Lab and the Footprints section with personal storytelling, we turned what could have been a boring history lesson into an unforgettable adventure of discovery.

Factors our team considered:

We designed Forgotten in Orbit with a first-time visitor always in mind. Instead of giving people long, complicated pages to read, we built a clean, responsive layout that works effortlessly on any screen. We kept the storytelling light and easy for younger readers to enjoy, while grounding every timeline and technical detail in real facts.
